messages:
anya: quick design review — thinking through the pool picklist order and SLO slider copy. dropped a Figma and a short vid: https://figma.com/file/xyz

jess: looked — main thing i noticed is the picklist groups feel equal weight. most teams pick 'general-purpose' and 'low-latency' 80% of the time. can we surface those to the top by default?

mike: we can sort by usage + pinned pools for orgs, but backend needs stable ids if we reorder dynamically. prefer a primary/secondary grouping UI rather than full sort.

anya: yeah — primary/secondary grouping sounds good. suggestion: show two rows in the dropdown: "Recommended" (top) + "All pools" below. reduces cognitive load.

jess: agree. UI nits: the selected pool chip currently shows just name. can we add a small SLO badge (e.g., "SLO: 99ms") so you know the default latency tier at a glance? small icon only, not full text.

omar: a11y note — if we add badges/icons, ensure they have accessible labels. e.g., aria-label="Pool: low-latency, SLO 99ms" and don't rely on color alone for tier meaning. Also contrast on the badge background is low in the artboard.

mike: noted. on metrics we can expose the SLO string for the badge component, aria label is straightforward.

lee: copy question: we currently call the extra capacity "Burst" in UI. customers keep asking if burst is paid separately. maybe change microcopy to "Temporary burst capacity" or add a help tooltip: "Temporary burst capacity: short-lived extra GPUs during spikes." Thoughts?

jess: prefer tooltip + shorter label: "Burst (temporary)" — keeps compactness but clarifies. update the help text: one sentence + link to billing FAQ.

anya: +1 to tooltip. also guardrails: we have an SLO slider in the mock that sets min/max tokens per second target. Could use better labels — avoid technical jargon. e.g., call it "Latency target" with presets: "Best-effort, Balanced, Low latency (SLO)". when low-latency is selected, we show an inline explanation: "Uses higher baseline capacity; costs may increase."

khalid: UX accessibility: the slider needs keyboard-friendly stepper fallback. When you tab to it, arrow left/right should adjust and the value should announce via aria-live. Also ensure the preset chips are focusable buttons, not divs.

omar: +1 for aria-live. Also for screen readers add "Current selection: Low latency, estimated cost: +15%" — so users understand cost impact without relying on tooltips that are hover-only.

mike: implementation constraint: we can only estimate cost in buckets (low/med/high) not precise %. Will surface as "estimated cost: higher" or explicit tier text. ok?

anya: that's fine. prefer plain language. change proposal: badge shows "Cost: higher" or "Cost: lower". keep the percent out.

jess: tiny copy nit on min/max steppers — replace "min"/"max" labels with "Min active GPUs" and "Max active GPUs" for clarity. ensure label is programmatically associated with the input (for attribute or aria-labelledby).

khalid: stepper voiceover: announce when the pool doesn't allow the requested min (we clamp). speech: "Requested min 8 clamped to pool max 4." Keep it short.

arya-bot: (deploy-bot) Figma link updated to include accessibility tokens: https://figma.com/file/xyz?rev=3

jess: one more: keyboard help text under the slider like "Left/right to adjust. Enter to confirm." small and visible only on focus.

anya: great feedback — next steps: jess to iterate mock with grouping + SLO badge, add tooltip copy. mike to confirm ID stability approach for recommended grouping. omar and khalid to review a11y tokens after the next mock. i'll coordinate release notes copy for the change.

mike: ok will validate backend ids and post constraints here by EOD.

omar: will do a quick a11y pass once the Figma rev is up.

jess: i'll post updated frames by tomorrow morning.

lee: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

anya: thanks — filing a tiny PRD for the rollout and canary flags now.
